label: Q1 close-out: the surface order is encoded only in authored hub data (hub-router.json:7 tieBreak ranks sk-code-opencode ahead of both examples; the set is declared, not ranked, at mode-registry.json:19 and SKILL.md:40), and ROUTER.md 265-618 encodes no order - 0 matches for tieBreak/order phrases; the surfaces appear there only as a scoring class (:346 OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN) and per-class resource lists (:354-523, :555-558, :607).

A user surface appended to the shipped tieBreak is valid yet loses every tie: opencode sits at index 2 of 5 (hub-router.json:7, re-verified) and sibling validators compare mode sets, not order (carried iteration-006.md:22).

The shipped data still treats both examples as installed for routing: routerSignals entries all weight 4 (webflow :31, opencode :36, obsidian :42), registry surface entries (:61-77, :79-95, :98-114), SKILL.md:40 exactly three surfaces, ROUTER.md:346 and :555-558 resource classes, plus the carried README and v4.0.0.4 note lines.

Break baseline every fix must answer (carried, copy-observed): deletion gives parent-skill-check exit 1 with 113 invariant failures (3c x2, 5d, 10a MODE_LEAF_SET_COLLISION, 12a x109) and fleet gate RRC-006; addition gives five new FAILs (3d-files, 6b, 5k-alias, 5k-packet, 5k-canary; 113 to 118); a hand edit without a working re-mint serves the legacy stub.

Q6 rejection list: reject a new operator-vs-external config file, a plugin system, a native/fallback flag, removing the examples from the operator repo, the docs-only insertion convention, --surface-hint as the default, deriving order from the installed set, checker-only downgrades, and an examples schema list - each has a cheaper covering move (rank data plus derived tieBreak; the documented scaffold; data defaults plus keep-local; docs markers).

Ranked recommendation set: R1 rank field per surface in mode-registry.json plus a tieBreak derived at mint (recommended); R2 ship-without-examples default data edit paired with R1; R3 doc example markers; R4 keep --surface-hint as the zero-code complement; R5 update-engine and scaffold doc follow-ups after R1/R2. Phases: Phase 0 full-tree re-mint verification (unobserved prerequisite), Phase 1 docs, Phase 2 rank plus derivation, Phase 3 shipped-default edit plus operator process.

direction: New operator-vs-external config file or engine layer
reason: No such layer exists and the engine's decisions machinery is uniform per checkout; the split the file promises is already data (Q4), so it duplicates the machinery without ranking anything.
Surfaces are already registry plus packet data read by the mint; the documented scaffold path ships, and an API is a second path to the same registry entry (two-real-callers bar).

direction: Hard-coded operator order behind a flag (native/fallback boolean on opencode)
reason: One boolean cannot give two repositories different orders and forces the operator's repo to the same order (iteration 6 option B).

direction: Removing obsidian and webflow from the operator repo
reason: The operator's tree is the release source; removing them removes the examples from the shipped release, and removal is unnecessary because the shipped-default edit is a data change.

direction: Docs-only insertion convention for tieBreak and routerSignals
reason: Two lists must agree and already drifted in a sibling hub; insertion position is unenforced; a hand edit serves the legacy stub until a working re-mint.

direction: --surface-hint as the shipped default tie fix
reason: Runtime-only, opt-in, matched-only: an unmatched surface can never lead, so it cannot be the default; it works as the complement.

direction: Deriving the order from the installed packet set at mint
reason: Compiled artifacts become environment-dependent and no installed-set input exists; the update engine computes file status, not routing order.

direction: Checker-only downgrade of absent example surfaces (blanket WARN or a new example check)
reason: No example marker exists in the engine and a blanket WARN would silence 3c, the check that catches a genuinely half-deleted user surface.

direction: examples schema list plus WARN on absent example dirs
reason: Same outcome as the shipped-default data edit for users who ship without the examples; schema growth fails the two-real-callers bar because only the operator wants them shipped.
